overlays.notes: Measured 2026-07-13 from the protocol's own stats API: total collateral value $71,324,392 against total BOLD supply 29,047,740 gives a system collateralization ratio of 2.455; Stability Pool deposits of 19,111,283 BOLD against the same supply give a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.658. The dedicated qualitative review on 2026-07-15 used Liquity's current documentation and implementation pinned at commit c8a5a4ee2e9dc024905856b6698a77d849c68c7e. Each branch has its own Stability Pool; liquidation burns deposited BOLD against debt and redistributes any remainder only among active Troves in that branch. That establishes an adequate two-stage backstop and adequate operational branch isolation, while the shared BOLD claim still exposes holders to unrecovered debt from any branch and prevents a strong rating. A branch can permanently shut down below its SCR or on oracle failure, stop interest and new borrower operations, and enable urgent branch redemptions. Liquity's own risk disclosure nevertheless states that collapsed collateral can leave unbacked BOLD with no unconditional recapitalization facility, so shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited. Any BOLD holder can permissionlessly redeem through the CollateralRegistry for a routed mix of collateral at protocol value, with urgent redemption available after branch shutdown, supporting adequate structural redemption.

StabilityPool.getTotalLUSDDeposits() over getEntireSystemDebt() gives a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.278; LUSD totalSupply() equals getEntireSystemDebt() exactly at the pinned block, so the ratio is identical against supply. checkRecoveryMode() was false, MCR 110%, CCR 150%. The pinned implementation and official documentation establish that Stability Pool deposits burn liquidated debt and that any residual debt and collateral are redistributed across active Troves, supporting an adequate backstop design while the measured 27.8% committed-capital ratio remains visible. Liquity V1 is one immutable ETH-only Trove system, so cross-branch isolation is structurally not applicable. Recovery Mode changes liquidation rules but the protocol has no shutdown or unconditional recapitalization facility, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt quality. Any holder can permissionlessly redeem LUSD for protocol-priced ETH from the lowest-collateralized Troves, supporting adequate structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Measured on-chain 2026-07-14 at HyperEVM block 40440545 via eth_call. The contract graph was derived on-chain: the feUSD token exposes no Liquity getters (it is a role-gated upgradeable ERC20, not Liquity's BoldToken), so the graph was taken from the CollateralRegistry proxy 0x9de1e57 (impl 0xD06DfC33), whose totalCollaterals() = 4 and getTroveManager(i)/getToken(i) enumerate exactly four branches: WHYPE (TM 0x3100F4e7), UBTC (TM 0xbbe5f227), kHYPE (TM 0x7c07bB77), wstHYPE (TM 0x58446C58). The registry address is corroborated by Felix's own docs, and each TroveManager's activePool() matches the four holders already in the coin file's liveReservesConfig. Per branch, getEntireBranchColl() x PriceFeed.lastGoodPrice() over getEntireBranchDebt(): WHYPE 430,173.636 WHYPE @ $65.20795344 = $28,050,742 vs debt 9,522,352.500 (CR 2.946); UBTC 28.055 @ $62,449.56855 = $1,752,006 vs debt 569,059.981 (CR 3.079); kHYPE 75,231.740 @ $64.98626 = $4,889,029 vs debt 1,123,782.912 (CR 4.351); wstHYPE 10,395.891 @ $65.41448 = $680,042 vs debt 348,425.553 (CR 1.952). System totals: collateral $35,371,819 over total branch debt 11,563,620.946 feUSD = collateralizationRatio 3.059. Cross-checks: (1) Felix's TroveManager has no getTCR(uint256), so collateral was verified three ways — TroveManager.getEntireBranchColl() equals ActivePool.getCollBalance() equals the collateral ERC20's balanceOf(ActivePool) for all four branches (exact, to within 1 wei on WHYPE); (2) re-valuing the same collateral at the live PriceFeed.fetchPrice() instead of lastGoodPrice() gives CR 3.070, agreeing to within 0.4%; (3) total branch debt 11,563,620.946 versus feUSD totalSupply() 11,563,588.435 agree to 0.0003% — supply is 32.51 feUSD BELOW debt, which is the expected direction for Liquity V2 (branch debt includes interest accrued but not yet minted), not a discrepancy. DefiLlama independently reports 11,563,600.69 circulating. liquidationCapacityRatio = sum of StabilityPool.getTotalfeUSDDeposits() (the fork's rename of getTotalBoldDeposits) 9,915,239.353 over total debt = 0.857; each pool's deposits plus getYieldGainsOwed() reconcile exactly against feUSD.balanceOf(StabilityPool), confirming the deposit figure is committed capital actually held, not an accounting claim. IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: Stability Pools are branch-local and cannot cross-subsidize, and coverage is very uneven — UBTC's pool holds 3.572x its own branch debt while wstHYPE holds only 0.238x and WHYPE 0.703x. Capping each branch's usable pool at its own debt gives a branch-isolation-adjusted ratio of 0.731; the reported 0.857 is the brief's uncapped sum-over-total definition and is the optimistic bound. Parameters read on-chain from each BorrowerOperations: MCR 135% / CCR 170% / SCR 120% for WHYPE, kHYPE and wstHYPE, and MCR 125% / CCR 150% / SCR 120% for UBTC. All four branches are live (shutdownTime() = 0) and on their primary oracle (PriceFeed priceSource = 0, i.e. not fallen back to lastGoodPrice). Liquidation penalties are not exposed by any public getter. Felix's docs and pinned implementation establish an independent state contract per branch, a branch-local Stability Pool with residual debt and collateral redistributed only to that branch's active troves, system redemption through the CollateralRegistry, and SCR-triggered branch shutdown with urgent redemption. Backstop and branch isolation are adequate; structural redemption is adequate. Shutdown and bad-debt handling are limited because shutdown, urgent redemption, and redistribution are implemented, but no separate recapitalization facility covers a branch-wide collateral deficit and the documented external control is Anthias monitoring.

The pinned PoolManager implementation gives EMERGENCY_ROLE a protocol pause, permits a DEBT_REDUCER_ROLE to burn supplied fxUSD while reducing pool debt, and lets the short-pool counterparty settle shortfall by reducing long-pool collateral and invalidating residual credit notes. Normal redemption is disabled while paused, although counterparty-only settlement redemption remains available, and the implementation establishes no unconditional external recapitalization facility. These bounded emergency and bad-debt paths support limited shutdownAndBadDebt quality.

overlays.notes: Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25536894; journaled evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/reusd-resupply/2026-07-15-block-25536894.json. The registry enumerated 19 unique pairs and their collateral vault conversions; active-pair collateral over debt gives 1.078969, with debt and token supply diverging 0.0304%. Three zero-debt pairs remain enumerated but their converted assets are excluded from the system ratio. InsurancePool reUSD held against debt gives 0.100629 committed liquidation capacity. Collateral is a layered ERC-4626 claim on crvUSD/frxUSD lending markets valued at protocol accounting par, not proof of immediate underlying liquidity. The pinned LiquidationHandler records uncovered debt by collateral and can clear it only when recovered collateral or InsurancePool assets are sufficient, while owner-directed distribution can socialize impaired collateral to InsurancePool holders; this is a defined but limited bad-debt path without unconditional recapitalization or global settlement. The pinned RedemptionHandler lets holders redeem pair debt directly only when its owner-configurable guard is disabled or the reUSD oracle price falls below the permissionless threshold; otherwise only the protocol redemption operator may call it. Same-transaction communal redemption therefore exists, but its conditional access and configurable fees support limited structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25536894; journaled evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/gho-aave/2026-07-15-block-25536894.json. All six facilitator bucket levels sum exactly to 599,000,000 GHO total supply, proving issuance allocation rather than collateral adequacy. Shared multi-debt Aave accounts have no honest GHO-only system collateralization ratio, and external liquidators are not a GHO-dedicated committed pool, so both requested ratios are structurally N/A. Unused facilitator capacity is 0.447412 of supply but is governance mint authority, not backstop capital. The two directly inspected, unfrozen and unseized GSMs provide a non-exhaustive swappable-capacity lower bound of 0.099750. Governance-set per-facilitator bucket caps provide bounded issuance isolation, but they do not make GHO losses fully facility-remote. Umbrella then automates first-loss-offset and staker coverage for supported asset-network pairs, including GHO on Ethereum, but current coverage is not established across every measured facilitator. System collateralization ratio 1.645315 = 56170191.00 CHF computed collateral value (open, non-denied position balances valued at price-mapping CHF prices) over total supply; the protocol's own TVL cross-check (56689834.48 CHF, 0.92% higher) gives 1.660537 and the position-debt-only variant 1.674787. Position-level parameters are explicit per the positions documentation and API: owner-set liquidation price bounding mintable debt, per-position minimum collateral, per-position reserve contribution (observed 10%-40% of minted, mostly 20%-25%), 1%-3% annual interest, and mostly one-day challenge periods; new minters pass a 14-day application with qualified pool-share holder veto (>2% of holding-period-weighted votes). No protocol-enforced minimum collateral ratio beyond the owner-set liquidation price was found; sound pricing is enforced ex-post through challenges, supporting adequate rather than strong collateralization parameters. Liquidation runs through permissionless challenge auctions whose bid-switching design (bids above the liquidation price buy the challenger's collateral instead of the position's) makes price manipulation expensive, with a 2% challenger reward and no oracle dependency: adequate liquidation mechanics whose own documentation states the assumption that challengers can acquire the collateral asset, and no committed bidder of last resort exists. Bids are externally funded and no ZCHF-dedicated pool is contractually committed to debt offset, so liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not applicable; the measured reserve pool is loss-absorption capital and is reported as analogous metrics instead. Backstop: the reserve documentation and pinned source establish three loss layers - the challenged position's minter reserve contribution, then FPS equity, then the general minter reserve - with coverLoss minting uncovered ZCHF as the terminal backstop; at block 25538909 the reserve pool held 12748870.64 ZCHF = 37.34% of supply (minter reserve 8634455.93 = 25.29%, FPS equity 4114414.71 = 12.05%; FPS market cap about $12.34M), supporting adequate backstop. NOT established: any stress-tested bound on reserve adequacy against the tokenized-equity collateral lines (BOSS is about 31% of collateral value), and the terminal backstop is dilutive inflation rather than pre-funded capital. Branch isolation: each position is a separate contract holding exactly one collateral type, and a failed position's collateral cannot be seized for another position's debt; cross-branch transmission exists only through the shared FPS equity and general minter reserve after a position's own reserve is consumed - adequate. NOT established: any per-collateral debt ceiling limiting one collateral line's share of system debt. Shutdown and bad debt: no global settlement or shutdown mechanism exists; bad debt is socialized through coverLoss, whose pinned source shows the reserve pool absorbing first and any uncovered remainder being minted as new ZCHF - limited. Structural redemption: holders have no direct redemption claim on position collateral; structural exits are the 1:1 stablecoin bridges (XCHF/VCHF/CHFAU, per-bridge limits and horizons) and secondary markets, while auctions repay position debt rather than holder claims - limited. NOT established: any holder-level redemption path to collateral.

overlays.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-20. K3's technical documentation establishes sBOLD as a standard-conforming ERC-4626 vault whose underlying asset is BOLD, deployed across multiple Liquity V2 Stability Pools at pre-configured basis-point weights; collateral gains from liquidations are quoted in real time and swapped to BOLD through a SwapAdapter with a documented minimum-quantity formula (max slippage, reward and swap fee each capped at 10%), and deposit/withdraw preview rounding always favors the vault. Measured on-chain at Ethereum block 25572100 via eth_call: totalAssets() = 7,848,262.699387884 BOLD, totalSupply() = 7,305,521.922387332 sBOLD, convertToAssets(1e18) = 1.074291855 BOLD per share. The wrapper originates no borrower debt and operates no collateral-ratio liquidation branches, so both CDP metrics and the collateralization and liquidation components are structurally not applicable; liquidation execution itself is inherited from the parent BOLD system (variantOf bold-liquity, reviewed separately). Because the vault allocates across several Stability Pools pro-rata, bad debt in any one pool transmits to the shared NAV by design and the configured weights are not published in the reviewed documentation, so branch isolation is limited. The documentation itself conditions the compounding-share behavior on 'no bad debt from unsuccessful liquidations', i.e. unsuccessful-liquidation losses pass through to the share rate with no wrapper-level cure, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt. Redemption is a standard ERC-4626 redeem, but the redeemed value depends on oracle-quoted collateral conversion executed by K3's mutable solver/swap infrastructure under a 2/3 Safe admin, supporting limited structural redemption. NOT established: the current per-pool allocation weights, withdrawal behavior under Stability Pool withdrawal stress, the full admin/pause control inventory, and any backstop standing behind the wrapper itself (sBOLD is itself risk-absorption capital for BOLD, so no separate backstop component is curated).

collateralizationRatio.rationale: sBOLD is an ERC-4626 allocator over Liquity V2 Stability Pools; it originates no borrower debt and has no collateralized vault system of its own, so a system collateralization ratio is structurally undefined at the wrapper level.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: sBOLD has no debt of its own to offset; its deposits are themselves liquidation capital committed to the parent BOLD system, so a wrapper-level liquidation capacity ratio is structurally not applicable.

collateralizationParameters.rationale: The vault takes BOLD deposits and allocates them to Stability Pools; it has no borrower collateral positions or collateral-ratio thresholds.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: Liquidation execution is inherited from the parent Liquity V2 BOLD system; the wrapper only allocates deposits into Stability Pools and swaps accumulated collateral gains back to BOLD.

The whitelisted basket, per-asset exposure targets, and adaptive fee schedule are documented and the Ethereum Parallelizer diamond's minter role and collateral list were verified on-chain 2026-07-20, supporting adequate collateralization parameters. Permissionless anytime proportional redemption at oracle value supports adequate structural redemption, subject to the documented whitelist caveat for restricted collateral assets. The documented below-100% redemption penalty is a socialized, fee-based recapitalization path rather than an insurance fund, and pause/guardian powers sit with DAO governance and a team multisig, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt. overlays.notes: Measured on-chain 2026-07-20 at pinned HyperEVM block 40944159 via eth_call (evidence: agents/tmp/mech3-parts/evidence/cdp-b.json). Pool.getReservesList() returned 19 reserves; per reserve, getReserveData gave the configuration bitmap (LTV bits 0-15) and the aToken/variableDebtToken pair, and each aToken totalSupply() was valued at HyFiOracle.getAssetPrice(). Collateral-eligible (LTV>0) supplies totaled 10,020,875.41 USD (10,126,165.91 USD including collateral-disabled USDXL, USDe, and feUSD supplies) against 2,902,469.67 USD of pool-wide variable debt, a pooled collateralization ratio of 3.452534 (3.488810 including disabled assets). USDXL variable debt in the pool was 108,924.2466 at an oracle price of 1.00; USDXL totalSupply was 160,758.035524. Because the Aave V3 fork mutualizes collateral across all borrow assets, USDXL debt cannot be separately collateral-attributed; the reported ratio is the whole-pool measure and includes 2.19M USD of WHYPE-denominated debt alongside the USDXL slice. Per-reserve parameters measured: LTV 20-68% with liquidation thresholds 40-83% and 8-12% bonuses, plus documented eMode overrides (90/95/3 HYPE-correlated, 90/93/3 USD-correlated), supporting adequate collateralization parameters. Liquidation is the standard permissionless Aave V3 liquidationCall, immediate below health factor 1 with a 50% close factor (100% at or below 0.95) and a 50% protocol share of the bonus: adequate liquidation mechanics executed by externally funded liquidators, so no USDXL-dedicated pool is contractually committed to debt-offset liquidation and the liquidation capacity metric is not applicable. The reviewed deployed fork contains no Stability Pool, auction, insurance, or automatic deficit backstop, and the USDT0 PSM (the only reserve-backed swap path) held 0 USDT0 at the pinned block: weak backstop. All 16 collateral reserves share one pooled market, so losses in any reserve socialize across the same debt pool with no isolation: weak branchIsolation. Pool roles can freeze or pause reserves and most reserves were measured frozen in the announced wind-down (markets targeted to close 2026-07-15), but the deployed Pool lacks V3.3 deficit APIs and has no automatic residual-debt elimination: limited shutdownAndBadDebt. HypurrFi's own documentation states direct redemptions are not currently enabled, and the measured zero PSM inventory confirms no current fixed-price exit: weak structural redemption. NOT established: per-position collateral attribution to the USDXL debt slice; the size and custody of the claimed protocol-owned USDT0/USDXL liquidity reserve; and any post-wind-down settlement or migration plan for residual debt.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: USDXL debt is liquidated through the pooled Aave V3 liquidationCall executed by externally funded liquidators; no USDXL-dedicated pool is contractually committed to debt-offset liquidation.

All nine debt-bearing uUSD engines from the pinned registry were enumerated; per-engine collateral is the sum of vault_contexts balances (validated exactly against the USDt V3 engine's FA2 token balance) and debt is the engine total_supply, whose sum across engines equals the uUSD token totalSupply 11,694,001.972561449 exactly. Valued at the protocol's own Ubinetic composite prices at the same level (USDTUSD 0.99862, XTZUSDT 0.2263, BTCUSDT 65117.16, and the SIRS LP ratio oracle 961987432172 read as 9.62e-7 tzBTC per SIRS = $0.0626), total collateral is $14,657,431.98 against debt of 11,694,001.97 uUSD: collateralizationRatio 1.253415. The SIRS price is the one unresolved valuation input: the LP ratio oracle implies $0.0626 per SIRS while current pool reserves (15.31 tzBTC against 29.46M SIRS) imply $0.0338, a 1.85x divergence; a vault-health test on all 84 debt-bearing SIRS V3 vaults (1 of 84 below the 135% minimum at the oracle price versus 8 of 84 at the pool price) supports the oracle price as the engine-operative one, and the pool-derived conservative variant would give 1.221910. Per-branch minimum collateral ratios (USDt 110%, tzBTC/SIRS 135%, XTZ 160%, legacy 200% emergency) are enforced on mint and withdrawal by the pinned base_tracker_engine_v3 and matched finalized storage: adequate collateralizationParameters. Liquidation is permissionless and atomic with payout capped at actual vault ratio or the configured payout, but the legacy SIRS branch was observed fail-closed (PRICE_TOO_OLD after 301 stale epochs) at level 14059094 and eight branches accept millisecond oracle timestamps against a seconds-based nominal 900-second freshness check, so liquidationMechanics is limited. backstop is limited: no Stability Pool, insurance reserve, or debt auction is connected to any engine, and the issuer documents the bailout/minter conversion right as inactive for new vaults and savings pools. branchIsolation is adequate: the nine engines are separate per-collateral contracts with their own oracles, ratios, and vaults, and unrecovered debt remains vault- and engine-local with no cross-branch socialization. shutdownAndBadDebt is limited: no shutdown, settlement, or deficit-redistribution module exists, so uneconomic debt persists vault-locally. structuralRedemption is limited: the documented holder conversion right lets holders convert against the lowest-collateralized vault at the settlement ratio (115% USDt, 200% crypto branches, parameters verified in storage) but carries a 24-hour announcement period, a vault opt-out surface for newer engines, and no observed settlement volume. Not established: per-vault target ratios above the enforced minimums (aggregates only), savings-pool balances and any liquidation capacity they might provide (no liquidationCapacityRatio is reported because liquidations are funded by external callers burning their own uUSD with no committed pool to measure), and the resolution path for the SIRS oracle/pool price divergence.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: All nine debt-bearing Youves engines liquidate through permissionless external callers who burn their own uUSD; no stability pool, insurance reserve, or debt auction commits capital to debt-offset liquidation, and the issuer documents the legacy bailout conversion feature as inactive, so there is no committed liquidation capacity to measure.

overlays.notes: 2026-07-20 review. Zephyr Protocol is a Monero-fork chain running a Minimal-Djed reserve design: ZSD is minted and redeemed directly against the ZEPH base coin held in the on-chain protocol reserve, and ZRS reserve shares form the equity/first-loss tranche. There are no borrowing positions and no liquidations in the design — peg defense is mint gating plus an always-permitted redemption path — so the liquidationMechanics component and the liquidationCapacityRatio metric are structurally not-applicable. Whitepaper rules: new ZSD cannot be minted when the reserve ratio is below 400% (dual spot and moving-average ratios must both pass, an anti-manipulation variation on stock Djed); ZRS minting halts above 800% to prevent dilution; the ZRS price falls toward PminRC below 400% to incentivize recapitalization; redeem_stable is always permitted, paying oracle value while the reserve ratio is >= 1 and a pro-rata share of the reserve if it ever falls below 1 (stable-holder haircut as the terminal bad-debt rule). Post-audit hardfork v11 renamed asset types to ZPH/ZSD/ZRS/ZYS per the protocol documentation. MEASUREMENT from the protocol's own reserve snapshot API (captured 2026-07-19T23:46:28Z at reserve_height 822991): ZEPH reserve 4,450,016.09, ZSD circulation 422,029.10, ZRS circulation 2,632,087.36, spot price $0.46573515 per ZEPH; reserve assets = 4,450,016.09 x 0.46573515 = $2,072,528.91 against $422,029.10 ZSD liabilities (equity $1,650,499.79) giving the protocol-reported reserve_ratio of 4.910867 on spot and 4.537806 on the moving average. collateralizationRatio is reported as the spot reserve ratio 4.910867; the moving-average figure 4.537806 is the binding mint-gate value. NOT ESTABLISHED: the snapshot API is the protocol's own self-reported scanner and no independent third-party attestation of the reserve was found; the oracle operator set and its decentralization were not established; ZRS secondary-market depth (real recapitalization capacity) was not established; no shutdown or wind-down mechanism exists in the design.
